description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
Release candidate. Fixes for reading and writing the same dataset at the same time, most of which
      returned wrong results without an error rather than failing, and for a facet panel that counted
      the documents as they were before an insert or delete. Found by tests that run searches, filter
      loads or vector searches beside inserts and updates; each fix below was reproduced that way unless
      it says otherwise. Nothing stored needs converting. One removal: the obsolete `Indx.CloudApi`
      aliases, below. One rule made explicit: the field's type decides the filter kind, and a filter
      of the other kind is refused; see the first entry. Two additions: a flag on `ValueFilterProxy`,
      and `Index()` on a disposed engine answering through the monitor.
      
      - Changed: **a range filter needs a field whose values are numbers, and a value filter a field
        whose values are not.** `CreateRangeFilter` on a text field - which is what a number stored as
        a JSON string is - returns null with the fix in `error`: store the values as numbers and load
        again. `CreateValueFilter` on a numeric field returns null with the filter to use instead: a
        range with equal limits, which compares as numbers and reads the field's index. Both used to
        be accepted and answered by walking every document; the range over text was correct and
        O(documents) for every new range, the value over a number compared JSON text and missed
        `129.0` when asked for `129`. A serialized key of the refused kind no longer rebuilds
        (`GetFilterFromKey` returns null), so a client holding such a token re-creates the filter.
      - Changed: `Index()` that built the search index but could not build the per-field filter
        indexes reports it as the call's failure: `Succeeded` false and the reason on the monitor, an
        `InvalidOperationException` on the synchronous path. The engine is Ready and searches;
        filters are built by walking the documents until the next `Index()`. This used to be a bare
        catch with nothing to show for it.
      - Changed: a score the 16-bit encoder cannot represent is clamped both ways and counted, where a
        negative used to wrap to near the ceiling - the least significant term of a query then made the
        most confident-looking score, so a large part of a corpus could come back looking like perfect
        matches. The cause of those negatives is fixed; if one ever comes back,
        `ScoreEncodingDiagnostics` counts it and the engine logs one error per `Search` or `Index()` that
        saw it. Ordinary results are unchanged.
      - Changed: term-frequency handling now adapts to `Field.BM25k1` instead of assuming the default, so
        a field configured with a small k1 keeps more resolution than it did. Scores for the default k1
        are unchanged; a field carrying a non-default k1 may rank slightly differently.
      - Fixed: a filter load running at the same time as an insert could throw `NullReferenceException`.
        It affected only the filters that have to examine every document: a case-sensitive value
        filter, a filter on an array field, or one on a field made `Filterable` since the last `Index()`.
        A filter that can use the field's index, which is most of them, was never affected. Reproduced on
        ARM64, in three runs of ten, and fixed for every affected filter kind.
      - Fixed: an array field nobody configured still cost memory per element on every document. Every
        leaf of every array was stored for lookup, whether or not the field had a role, where a scalar
        without a role was skipped. On documents carrying long unconfigured arrays that ran to tens of
        megabytes on a corpus of moderate size. Array leaves now follow the scalar
        rule on every load path, the dynamic ops and the rebuild inside `Index()`. Nothing that is read
        has changed.
      - Fixed: waking a small dataset from the database took as long as the team's largest. No index
        served a single-dataset lookup, so each one scanned everything stored for that team. Where a team
        holds a lot, loading a dataset of a hundred documents took on the order of a second; it is now
        sub-millisecond, and a small dataset was the worst case. New databases get the index when they
        are created, and `SqLiteManager.EnsureDatasetIndex()` adds it to an existing one; the Indx server
        calls that at startup.
      - Added `FilterLoadDiagnostics.IndexedFieldLoads` and `ScanFieldLoads`: every value or range
        filter load, split by whether it read the field's posting index or walked the documents
        (array fields, case-sensitive value filters, a field made Filterable since the last `Index()`).
      
      - Removed the `[Obsolete]` aliases for the pre-rename HTTP shapes: `Indx.CloudApi.CloudQuery`,
        `Indx.CloudApi.FilterProxy` and its siblings, and `Indx.Api.ICloudSearchEngine`. Use the
        `Indx.Http` names (`QueryProxy`, `FilterProxy`, ...) and `IServerSearchEngine`; the JSON on the
        wire is unchanged. RC140926 said the aliases would stay until the next major version; they go in
        the release candidate instead, because nothing but the 5.0 betas ever shipped them, and a
        compile error naming the replacement is a better guide than a warning nobody reads.
      - Added `ValueFilterProxy.IsCaseSensitive`, off by default, for the server's `filters/value`
        endpoint. Facets count distinct stored values with their casing, so only a case-sensitive filter
        agrees with a facet count. `Value` is documented as a string, number or boolean.
      - Changed: `Index()` on a disposed engine no longer throws `ObjectDisposedException` from inside a
        lock. It reports through the monitor - `Succeeded` false, "Index called on a disposed engine" -
        the way `Search` already answers a disposed engine.
      - Fixed: `UpdateField` could throw "Stack empty" when a range filter on a scalar field had been
        deleted from the cache while a combination built on it stayed, and the updated value lay outside
        the range. The combination is now evaluated by asking its operands about the document, which is
        also how a value or range filter is evaluated on its own; the second implementation that did
        this by parsing the filter's key is gone.
      
      - Fixed: an empty search with facets - what a facet panel sends - counted the documents as they
        were before the last insert or delete. The result was cached and nothing cleared it on insert or
        delete, and the count walked deleted documents too, which also listed them among the records.
      - Fixed: a filter combined with `&`, `|` or `!`, or rebuilt from its key, could keep the answer it
        had before the documents changed. After a `Load`, a clone, or an `Index()` that reads a field into
        use for the first time, every cached filter is marked for reloading but keeps its old mask, and
        combinations were built from those old masks and marked current. Measured: `red | blue` on a
        field given its first role returned none of 26 documents after `Index()`. Combinations now wait
        for their operands to reload.
      - Fixed: a filtered search running while another thread loaded the same filter, for example during
        `LoadAllFilters`, could run unfiltered, or filter against a mask still being filled and return too
        few results. Rare, and dependent on a precise interleaving; on ARM64 the ordering of the two writes made it
        likelier. A search now reads the filter's mask when it checks it, and a mask is published only once
        complete.
      - Fixed: a filter loaded while an insert or update wrote to the same field could come back wrong.
        A range filter could throw "Collection was modified", in up to half the loads under a steady
        stream of `UpdateField`; a value filter on a document being updated could miss it, 2499 of 2500
        documents when a value was respelled from "Red" to "RED". The per-field posting indexes now take
        a lock, once per filter load and once per document update.
      - Fixed: reading a field while an insert or update brought a field name never seen before - a new
        field, or an array longer than any before, whose elements each have a name - could find the field
        missing for a document. A filter scan missed up to 78 of 1500 documents, with no error. Affects
        filters, facets, sorting and coverage alike.
      - Fixed: a vector or hybrid search beside inserts, updates or deletes of embedded documents could
        lose hits: a search on a document's own vector returned as few as none of its ten neighbours.
        `EmbeddingIndex` now takes a reader-writer lock, so vector searches still run side by side.
      - Fixed: `LoadAllFilters` could throw "Collection was modified" when filters were created or
        evicted while it ran.
      - Fixed: after a `Load` on an engine that already held data, a filter without a posting index - one
        built case-sensitive, or on an array field - matched none of the new documents, and `UpdateField`
        changed a document but left the filters answering as before, while returning true. The reload
        gave the engine a new document store and the filter layer kept reading the old one; it now
        empties the one store instead. A first `Load` was never affected.
      - Fixed, found by review and not reproduced: a search running when `Index()` or `LoadAsync` started
        could read the model or documents being rebuilt under it; a search that skipped the compaction
        lock after a dynamic op could, on ARM64, read a term's new document list beside its old weights;
        and an empty search beside an insert could, on ARM64, read a document not yet fully in the list.
        `Index()` still returns as soon as the build has started; the build waits for such searches.
title: IndxSearchLib
